A.explanation: 0.4 C would come from dividing current by time rather than multiplying, which reverses $Q = It$.

B.explanation: 2 C is the magnitude of the current in R in amperes, before multiplying by the 5 s time to get charge.

C.explanation: Kirchhoff's first law gives 2 A in wire R, so $Q = It = 2 \times 5 = 10 \text{ C}$.

D.explanation: 20 C adds the 1 A and 3 A to get 4 A, ignoring that P flows into and Q flows out of the junction.

hints: Notice the arrow directions at the junction: 1 A in P flows toward the dot and 3 A in Q flows away from the dot.
Use Kirchhoff's first law that total current entering a junction equals total current leaving it to find the size and direction of the current in R.
Then use $Q = It$ with your current for R and $t = 5 \text{ s}$ to find the charge in coulombs.
walkthrough: Identify the junction currents: $I_P = 1 \text{ A}$ flows into the junction and $I_Q = 3 \text{ A}$ flows out of the junction.
Apply Kirchhoff's first law: sum of currents entering = sum of currents leaving, so $1 + I_R = 3$ if $I_R$ is taken as entering.
Solve for wire R: $I_R = 3 - 1 = 2 \text{ A}$ toward the junction, so the magnitude past any point in R is $2 \text{ A}$.
Use charge-current relation $Q = It$ with $I = 2 \text{ A}$ and $t = 5 \text{ s}$.
Substitute: $Q = 2 \times 5 = 10 \text{ C}$, with units $\text{A s} = \text{C}$. This is option C.
